description:
Solo participant with a BS in Physics and currently pursuing an MS in AI & Data Science. Combining astrophysics domain knowledge with machine learning.

 I built a cross-calibration pipeline that harmonizes historical ESA Hipparcos star brightness data (HIP 60202) with NASA Kepler Space Telescope spectral channels to eliminate sensor bias and support multi-mission exoplanet detection.
summary:
Space telescopes use different sensors and filters, causing two missions observing the same star to record slightly different brightness values. To help astronomers combine multi-mission data and detect orbiting exoplanets. I built an astrophysics cross-calibration pipeline harmonizing historical ESA Hipparcos observations with NASA Kepler Space Telescope spectral channels.Using Python, I cleaned 98 verified brightness records for star HIP 60202 alongside spectral response steps from NASA’s Kepler camera. 
I trained a Random Forest regression model to learn the star’s three-year brightness trend, achieving a low prediction error of 0.01109 magnitude. Simulating the star’s light across Kepler Channel 1 (0.3886 transmission) and Channel 29 (0.3883 transmission) proved how subtle sensor sensitivity shifts alter recorded flux. 
This framework bridges legacy and modern space telescope archives—supporting multi-mission astrophysics goals like Planet X and SPHEREx—so astronomers can reuse decades of star records without camera bias.
details:
The Problem
Instrument sensitivity differences across space telescope cameras cause slight offsets in recorded brightness when observing the same star, preventing astronomers from reliably combining historical archives with modern observations.
How It Works & Methodology
An end-to-end Python and machine learning pipeline harmonizes historical ESA Hipparcos photometry for star HIP 60202 with NASA Kepler Space Telescope spectral response channels:
  1. Data Extraction & Cleaning: Extracts 911 spectral wavelength steps across Kepler's channels and 98 high-quality epoch photometry observations for HIP 60202 using pypdf, pandas, and regular expressions.
  2. Machine Learning Trend Modeling: Trains a scikit-learn Random Forest Regressor on timestamps converted to days elapsed since BJD 2447875.91 to model the star's intrinsic light curve (RMSE of 0.01109 magnitude).
  3. Multi-Channel Sensor Simulation: Converts magnitudes into relative photon flux to simulate and quantify how light registers across different Kepler channels (e.g., Channel 1 and Channel 29).
Tools, Coding Languages & Libraries Used
  • Language & Environment: Python 3.12, Jupyter Notebook (NASA-MODEL.ipynb)
  • Data Processing & Machine Learning: pandas, numpy, scikit-learn (Random Forest Regressor), pypdf, re
  • Visualization: matplotlib (generating spectral response, light-curve trend, and simulated sensor flux plots)
NASA & Space Agency Data Used
  • NASA Kepler Mission Data (MAST / NASA Exoplanet Archive): Instrument spectral response curves and transmission tables across 911 wavelength steps.
  • ESA Hipparcos Catalogue (via NASA HEASARC / VizieR): Historical epoch photometry light-curve observations (\(H_{p}\) magnitude) for star HIP 60202.
Impact & Future Scope
Unites legacy and modern space telescope archives into a bias-free simulator to support multi-mission astrophysics (such as Planet X and SPHEREx) and scale automated batch-calibration for thousands of archival stars.
